questionText: What embedded servers does Spring Boot support and how do you switch between them?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can name Boot 3.3.1 server choices, replace the default starter correctly, and identify portable code and real selection boundaries without invented performance rankings.
inScope: Tomcat, Jetty, and Undertow for servlet applications
outOfScope: A claim that server choice changes MVC into WebFlux
prerequisites: Difference between Spring MVC and WebFlux

claims.statement: Spring Boot 3.3 supports embedded Tomcat, Jetty, and Undertow for servlet applications, with Tomcat selected by the web starter by default.
Spring WebFlux uses Reactor Netty by default and can also use supported servlet servers.
Switching a Spring MVC server requires excluding the Tomcat starter and adding the desired supported server starter.
Executable JAR packaging does not support JSP; Tomcat and Jetty can use JSP with WAR packaging, while Undertow does not support JSP.

examples.title: Maven dependency replacement from Tomcat to Jetty

validation.command: XML fence parsed with Python ElementTree and dependency coordinates checked
validation.expected: The dependency fragment is well-formed XML, excludes the Tomcat starter, and adds the Jetty starter

visuals.title: Spring MVC and WebFlux server choice table

notes: The comparison deliberately avoids unsupported claims that one server is always faster or smaller.

review.notes: Supported servers, defaults, dependency replacement, WebFlux options, and JSP boundaries were checked against official Spring Boot 3.3 web-server documentation.
